newsitem.title: UK: BAe, Rolls up on weekend press reports.
newsitem.headline: BAe, Rolls up on weekend press reports.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc and Rolls Royce Plc rose in pre-market trading on Monday after reports that the two companies were lobbying the British government to relax limits on foreign ownership of their shares.
BAe was up 8p at 1287-1/2 by 0809 GMT while Rolls Royce was up 2-1/2p at 261-1/2.
A report in the Sunday Times said the two companies believed the limit was outmoded, was an obstacle to shareholder value and could restrict their scope for strategic expansion.
It said overseas investors held about 26 percent of both companies and that scrapping the limit could release pent-up overseas demand.
Foreign shareholders are currently restricted to holding 29.5 percent of the companies.
Yet British Aerospace lost its early gain by the official start of trading, with the stock having difficulty building on Friday's near-record close.
The influential Lex column in Saturday's Financial Times said the stock looked "fully valued on fundamentals" since it was trading on a 10 percent premium to the rest of the UK market.
It said the euphoria over Boeing Co's bid for McDonnell Douglas Corp was overdone since "there is no European Boeing about to snap it up".
By 0833 GMT British Aerospace shares were up just 4p at 1283-1/2.
Analysts said the removal of the limit on foreign share ownership could be modestly positive for BAe and Rolls shares, but warned that hopes for a burst of overseas buying should not be overstated.
Zafar Khan, an analyst at SocGen, said the removal would be useful for simple policing reasons and that it could ease the way to any international alliances.
"But I think it would be incorrect to say that there is a huge number of guys waiting out there with their chequebooks open waiting to buy these shares," Khan said.

BAe spokesman Mike Peters said on Sunday that it would be advantageous if the foreign ownership limits no longer applied. "Both Rolls Royce and British Aerospace have had discussions with the government about the situation," Peters told Reuters. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
